lead.headline: Nvidia's board moves to oust Jensen Huang after a report of a second affair, this one with a senior employee
lead.short: Nvidia's board met on Wednesday night to decide the future of its co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang and is preparing to oust him, The Wall Street Journal reported. The New York Times reported that Huang, 63, had a second extramarital affair, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice-president of health care, with video of the two being affectionate at a hotel.

why.text: Nvidia's chips run the AI boom, and the man who built the company over three decades may be gone within days.

more: On Sunday the board had backed Huang and opened an independent investigation after he told staff "I was unfaithful to my wife" over his relationship with Alice Huang of Megaspeed, whom US intelligence believes worked for China's Ministry of State Security. Powell, 48, was speaking at a company conference in San Jose in March when bystanders saw the pair at the hotel, the Times said.

"Farewell Jensen," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG. "Huang might have been able somehow to cling on at Nvidia after one revelation, but after two, one of which involving a direct report, his fate is sealed." Shareholders have filed a class action over the affair, Congress has asked Huang for a closed-door briefing, and Nvidia's shares are falling.

facts.board: met Wednesday to decide Huang's future, per the WSJ
facts.second affair: with Kimberly Powell, vice-president of health care, per the NYT

update.new: The board is preparing to oust Huang after a second affair is reported.
update.front: Nvidia's founder is on the way out.

seconds.headline: Democrat Scott Colom wins in Mississippi to become its first Black senator since 1874, by fewer than 5,000 votes
seconds.short: Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, beating the Republican incumbent, Cindy Hyde-Smith, by fewer than 5,000 votes out of nearly a million. Colom, 43, is the first Black person from Mississippi elected to the Senate in more than 140 years. Democrats will hold 55 of the 100 seats, with Alaska still to be called.

why.text: A Democratic win in a state Trump carried by 22 points shows how far his party fell in last week's midterms.

more: Colom took 49.2% of the vote to Hyde-Smith's 48.7%, with an independent on 2.1%, according to CBS. "While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," Hyde-Smith said. The result ends a Republican winning streak in the state's Senate races that dates back to 1982.

"They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith," Colom told supporters at Tougaloo College. "It's not something that I did y'all. It's something we did." At the NAACP's office in Jackson, board chairman Leon Russell said: "There was not a whole lot of money, but there was a whole lot of organising."

update.new: Mississippi is called for the Democrat, giving the party 55 Senate seats.
update.front: A week after the midterms, the Democrats win a Senate seat in the Deep South for the first time in decades.

seconds.headline: Two special police officers missing in Kishtwar's forests are found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they vanished
seconds.short: Two Special Police Officers of the Jammu and Kashmir Police, part of an anti-terror operation, were found dead with bullet wounds on Thursday, a day after they went missing in a dense forest in the upper reaches of the Chenab Valley. They were SPO Rashpal Kumar, 45, and SPO Bobby Chand, 57, both from Kiyar Dachhan in Kishtwar.

why.text: It points to militants operating again in Jammu's hills, a day after an attack on the CRPF in Kashmir.

more: The two had accompanied a team from the Army's 17 Rashtriya Rifles to the Basnan area and failed to report back to their camp at Dharna on Wednesday, officials said. The area echoed with gunfire after they went missing, and their phones went silent. The bodies were found after a large search in the Kiyar sector of Dachhan.

Police have not issued a formal statement or confirmed that militants were involved. The SPOs were part of Temporary Operating Bases set up by the police after militant activity increased in the upper reaches of Jammu and Kashmir from 2020. A day earlier, militants fired on a CRPF checkpoint in Kulgam in south Kashmir, injuring three personnel.

facts.dead: SPOs Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Bobby Chand, 57

seconds.headline: A three-storey building in Brooklyn collapses into a construction site, killing at least two and injuring 17
seconds.short: At least two people died and more than 17 were injured when a three-storey building on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn collapsed into an open construction site at about 4pm on Wednesday. More than 250 first responders searched the rubble for people trapped from the building and the site, and firefighters pulled out a survivor hours later.

why.text: New York's building boom keeps putting new excavations next to old homes, and the city will want to know why this one gave way.

more: Fire Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore called the rescue "extremely dangerous". "Members have been working methodically and haven't stopped since they arrived this afternoon," she said. Pictures showed one whole side of the building gone, with bedrooms and closets open to the street and household items and clothes among the concrete and twisted metal.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani joined responders at the scene and said they "arrived in under a minute and have spent hours working in dangerous and highly technical conditions". The building dates from 1930, city records show, according to CBS News. Authorities have not yet said what caused the collapse.

stories.headline: India cuts its visa categories from 13 to nine and renames the tourist visa a visitor visa
stories.short: India has cut its main visa categories from 13 to nine and its sub-categories from 49 to 23, and made application forms up to 70% shorter, the Home Ministry said on Wednesday. The tourist visa is now a "visitor visa", covering a wider range of purposes, and a new production investment business visa covers foreign technical specialists.

why.text: Simpler visas make it easier for foreign engineers, investors and visitors to come, as India tries to draw factories and tourists.

more: The new business visa is for foreign subject specialists, engineers and technical staff hired by Indian companies for installation, commissioning, quality checks, maintenance, production, IT, training, plant design and transfer of know-how. The changes aim to make the system "more compact, coherent and responsive to the requirements of foreign nationals visiting India", the ministry said.

It follows an overhaul in October 2025, when the main categories were cut from 22 to 13 and the sub-categories from 63 to 49. The ministry said it studied the visa systems of developed countries and global standards, and that grouping similar purposes of travel would make it clearer which visa to apply for.

stories.headline: Indonesia's vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigns after courts reject his education documents
stories.short: Gibran Rakabuming Raka, Indonesia's 39-year-old vice-president and the son of former president Joko Widodo, resigned on Thursday after courts ruled that his overseas education documents did not meet election requirements. He handed his resignation to the People's Consultative Assembly in Jakarta, a day after 120 lawmakers from eight parties began a process that could have led to impeachment.

why.text: It ends a dynasty bet that began when a court ruling let him run though he was under the minimum age.

more: "There will always be political dynamics in public office, that's normal," Widodo told reporters in Solo. "We will continue to support President Prabowo's government." Raka had offered to resign on Tuesday in a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto, who urged him to defend himself, a Cabinet minister said.

Under Indonesia's constitution, the vacancy does not trigger an election: the assembly elects a replacement within 60 days from two candidates the president nominates. Raka did not meet the minimum age of 40 for the office before the 2024 election, and critics saw the Constitutional Court ruling that let him run as a conflict of interest.

stories.headline: Indian shares give up early gains as investors book profits, after foreign funds put ₹65,735 crore into stocks this month
stories.short: The Sensex rose 166 points to 82,013.58 in early trade on Thursday and then gave up the gain, standing 42.59 points lower at 81,836.81 at 12.12pm as investors booked profits near an eight-month high. Foreign institutional investors bought shares worth ₹12,563.33 crore on Wednesday and ₹65,735 crore so far in November, Geojit's V.K. Vijayakumar said.

why.text: Foreign money is driving India's best month in six years, and how long it keeps coming will decide whether the rally holds.

more: Insurers rose after the Life Insurance Council said first-year premium income grew 26.2% in October to ₹42,914 crore. Banks also gained, with ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank and SBI up 0.5% to 1.5%, while Nestle India fell nearly 2% and Bharti Airtel and Mahindra & Mahindra about 1%. The Nifty is up 9.6% and the Sensex 10% this month.

"This trend is likely to continue and has the potential to reach an all-time high number," Vijayakumar said of foreign buying, citing good second-quarter results and Brent crude at around $92. "Despite (Wednesday's) positive close, rejection from higher levels indicates some near-term profit booking," said Hitesh Tailor of Choice Broking.

update.new: The rally pauses for profit booking.

stories.headline: Bengaluru police recover hockey great M.M. Somaya's 1980 Olympic gold and seven other medals, and arrest two
stories.short: Indiranagar police have arrested two habitual offenders and recovered eight international medals stolen from the B.M. Kaval home of former India hockey player M.M. Somaya, including his gold from the 1980 Moscow Olympics. The family discovered the burglary after returning from their native Kodagu, where they had gone on 25 October.

why.text: The medals belong to one of the men behind India's last Olympic hockey gold before Tokyo.

more: The haul includes silver from the 1982 Asian Games, bronze from the 1986 Seoul Asian Games and the 1982 Champions Trophy in Amsterdam, and participation medals from the 1984 and 1988 Olympics. Police also recovered a traditional Kodava dagger, a camera, an Olympic kit bag and the two-wheeler used in the theft.

Eight special teams worked on the case. The accused, Manikya alias Manikanta, 31, a labourer, and Bharat, 25, were arrested near Hagalahalli Cross in Ramanagara on 9 November and confessed to the theft with a third man, police said. Manikanta has 33 criminal cases against him. The two had sold one gold and one silver medal, which were also recovered.

update.new: The medals are recovered and two men arrested.
